source.model: This is a sherpa-onnx ONNX export of Meta's facebook/omniASR-CTC-300M, not the original Meta/fairseq2 runtime implementation.

known_limitations: Confirmed architectural input-length limitation: degrades sharply past ~40s of continuous audio (Meta's own documentation, independently verified by direct testing at 10s/35s/60s/177s before running the benchmark). Required segmentation for this benchmark's 139-233s recordings -- a fixed chunking approach decided before running, not tuned afterward. No language-conditioning input exists for this model type (confirmed via official API signature) -- decoding is purely acoustic. Frequently omits word-boundary spaces within a single chunk's own output (a model/tokenization characteristic, confirmed NOT a stitching artifact by inspecting raw per-chunk output) -- inflates strict WER substantially more than CER or compound-aware WER, which forgive pure spacing differences.

source.checkpoint_source: OpenAI's official Whisper model registry -- the URL hardcoded in the openai-whisper package's own `_MODELS` dict for the "medium" alias, fetched automatically at run time (https://openaipublic.azureedge.net/main/whisper/models/345ae4da.../medium.pt). Not Hugging Face, not GitHub.
source.historical_invocation: whisper <audio_file> --language et --model medium --device cuda --output_format all --verbose False --output_dir .\benchmark\whisper
source.checkpoint_sha256_note: Exact match to the hash embedded in OpenAI's own published medium.pt download URL (openai-whisper package's _MODELS registry) -- confirmed by directly computing sha256sum of the locally cached checkpoint file, not inferred from filename or convention.
source.huggingface_cache_check: No Hugging Face cache entry for any Whisper model, generic or TalTechNLP, was present on the machine that ran this benchmark -- rules out a Hugging-Face-sourced checkpoint.
source.evidence_basis: PowerShell command history (literal invocation recovered), pip package installation metadata (INSTALLER=pip, package METADATA), and a direct SHA256 hash match against the locally cached checkpoint file. Full evidence trail recorded in project history; classified CONFIRMED, not inferred from naming.

known_unknowns: Decode used openai-whisper's own default beam-search/temperature-fallback behavior -- no --temperature or --beam_size override was passed in the recorded invocation, so defaults apply. known_unknowns: UNRESOLVED: the exact upstream/public provenance of the 'whisper-medium-et-v5-ct2' checkpoint baked into TalTech's est-asr-pipeline Docker image is not established from any local evidence -- it is not obtained via any visible download/build command in local history, only present inside a pre-built Docker image pulled from TalTech's own registry (not independently accessible outside TalTech's own infrastructure). Do NOT claim it is identical to the public TalTechNLP/whisper-medium-et Hugging Face model unless independently verified (e.g. by hashing the checkpoint file inside the Docker image and comparing) -- the 'v5' naming suggests a possibly further-iterated internal checkpoint, not necessarily what's published on HF. CONFIRMED DIFFERENT from the generic OpenAI Whisper medium checkpoint used by openai-whisper-medium-generic: separate pipeline (Docker/Linux vs. Windows Python venv), separate environment, and definitively not the same weights (see that system's source.checkpoint_sha256 -- OpenAI's stock checkpoint has a different, confirmed hash). Separately: known run-to-run variance in the GPU Whisper decode step -- the frozen 9.64% number is a single historical run, not yet characterized for variance itself.

source.model: OpenAI Whisper large-v3 -- generic, unmodified OpenAI checkpoint, NOT a TalTech fine-tune.
source.checkpoint_source: Systran's CTranslate2 conversion of openai/whisper-large-v3 (model card documents the exact ct2-transformers-converter command; MIT licensed; deterministic format conversion, no retraining).

known_limitations: Untuned generic large-v3 shows genuine repetition-loop hallucination on this benchmark (verbatim multi-sentence repeats observed in Set B, e.g. one sentence repeated 3-4 times), a known general Whisper failure mode, more visible here likely because VAD filtering is off (the untuned default) and the model has no Estonian-specific tuning to anchor confident decoding. This was observed, not fixed -- per instruction, no decoding parameters were tuned after seeing the result.
